args.text: --- title: 'Hello World' description: 'Change the FHE computation in the default template so that the E3 returns two times the sum, and run it again.' --- import { Callout, Steps } from 'nextra/components' import { Flow, LinkCard, LinkCards } from '@/components/ui' # Hello World Righto, in this one you'll tinker with the FHE computation in the default template and run the E3 again. It's for developers who've already knocked over the [Quick Start](/build/quick-start). By the end, your E3 spits out 2 × (a + b) instead of a + b, and you'll know which files hold the computation, its test, and its labels in the client. ## Before you begin You'll need the `my-first-e3` project from the [Quick Start](/build/quick-start), untouched. Every path on this page starts from the project folder. ## How the template computes The whole FHE computation is one Rust function, `fhe_processor`, in `program/src/lib.rs`. The rest of the template is just the delivery crew: it lugs ciphertexts to this function and carts its result off to the committee. 1. The client encrypts each number with the committee public key and calls `MyProgram.publishInput`. 2. Once the input window shuts, the coordination server (`server/index.ts`) reads the published inputs and fires them off to the program server on port 13151. 3. The program server (`.interfold/support/dev/src/main.rs`) calls `fhe_processor` and sends the encrypted result back to the coordination server. 4. The coordination server publishes the encrypted result, and the committee decrypts it. Here's the default computation in `program/src/lib.rs`, with the doc comment above `policy` taken out: ```rust filename="program/src/lib.rs" use e3_compute_provider::{FHEProcessorInput, InputPolicy}; use fhe::bfv::Ciphertext; use fhe_traits::{DeserializeParametrized, Serialize}; pub fn policy() -> InputPolicy { InputPolicy::default() } /// Implementation of the CiphertextProcessor function pub fn fhe_processor(fhe_inputs: FHEProcessorInput<'_>) -> Vec { let mut sum = Ciphertext::zero(fhe_inputs.params); for (bytes, _) in fhe_inputs.ciphertexts { let ciphertext = Ciphertext::from_bytes(&bytes, fhe_inputs.params).unwrap(); sum += &ciphertext; } sum.to_bytes() } ``` - `FHEProcessorInput` has two fields (the code kind, not paddocks). `ciphertexts` hands over `(Vec, u64)` pairs one at a time: the serialised ciphertext and its input index. `params` holds the BFV parameters of the E3. - `Ciphertext::zero` makes the zero ciphertext, the starting value. The `+=` operator adds each input ciphertext onto it. This addition is homomorphic: the function adds up the hidden values without ever getting a peek at them. Like counting votes in a sealed box. - `sum.to_bytes()` serialises the encrypted result. - `policy()` returns the input policy. The default policy takes every published input. The template asks for E3s with the `insecure-512` parameter set. Its plaintext modulus is 100, so every result is worked out modulo 100. For this tutorial, keep 2 × (a + b) under 100, or it'll wrap round on ya. ## Change the computation ### Stop the stack If `pnpm dev:all` is running, hit `Ctrl+C` in its terminal. ### Double the encrypted sum In `program/src/lib.rs`, swap the `fhe_processor` function out for this version: ```rust filename="program/src/lib.rs" {9-11} /// Implementation of the CiphertextProcessor function pub fn fhe_processor(fhe_inputs: FHEProcessorInput<'_>) -> Vec { let mut sum = Ciphertext::zero(fhe_inputs.params); for (bytes, _) in fhe_inputs.ciphertexts { let ciphertext = Ciphertext::from_bytes(&bytes, fhe_inputs.params).unwrap(); sum += &ciphertext; } // Add the encrypted sum to itself. The hidden value becomes 2 × (a + b). let doubled = &sum + ∑ doubled.to_bytes() } ``` `&sum + &sum` adds two ciphertexts and hands back a brand-spankin'-new ciphertext. No new imports needed, either. ### Update the unit test The test down the bottom of `program/src/lib.rs` encrypts 3 and 2 and calls `fhe_processor`. Bump the expected value from 5 to 10: ```rust filename="program/src/lib.rs" let tally = Vec::::try_decode(&decrypted, Encoding::poly())?; assert_eq!(tally[0], 10); Ok(()) ``` ### Run the unit test ```bash cargo test -p e3-user-program ``` Cargo prints `test tests::test ... ok`. If the test falls over, check your `fhe_processor` against the code in the step before. ### Update the label on the input step In `client/src/pages/steps/EnterInputs.tsx`, hunt down this line: ```tsx filename="client/src/pages/steps/EnterInputs.tsx" Ready to compute: {input1} + {input2} = ? ``` Change it to: ```tsx filename="client/src/pages/steps/EnterInputs.tsx" Ready to compute: 2 × ({input1} + {input2}) = ? ``` ### Update the label on the results step Over in `client/src/pages/steps/Results.tsx`, find this line: ```tsx filename="client/src/pages/steps/Results.tsx" { submittedInputs ? `${submittedInputs.input1} + ${submittedInputs.input2} = ${result !== null ? result : '…'}` : '…' } ``` Change it to: ```tsx filename="client/src/pages/steps/Results.tsx" { submittedInputs ? `2 × (${submittedInputs.input1} + ${submittedInputs.input2}) = ${result !== null ? result : '…'}` : '…' } ``` ### Start the stack ```bash pnpm dev:all ``` The `PROGRAM` process runs `interfold program start`. In dev mode, that command runs `cargo run --bin e3-support-scripts-dev`, so Cargo builds the program server again with your new `fhe_processor` baked in. ### Run an E3 Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). If the client's still showing the result of an earlier E3, hit **Start over** in the top bar. Request an E3, then punch in 5 and 3. The input step shows `Ready to compute: 2 × (5 + 3) = ?`. The results step shows `2 × (5 + 3) = 16`. Sixteen. Too easy. ## Why nothing else changes - **The contract.** `MyProgram.publishInput` stores a commitment for each input, and `MyProgram.verify` checks the compute proof. Neither one has the computation in it. - **The coordination server.** `server/index.ts` sends every published input to the program server and publishes whatever output comes back. It knows sweet bugger-all about what the computation does. - **The deployment.** `pnpm dev:all` deploys the contracts again on a fresh local chain every time it starts. In dev mode, the program server runs `fhe_processor` without a proof, and the template deploys `MockOpenVmReceiptVerifier`, which waves every receipt through on the local chain. With real proofs, `MyProgram.verify` checks the OpenVM receipt against the `imageId` that `MyProgram` gets handed when it's deployed. Change the program and you change that identity, so compile and deploy again. See [Compute provider](/build/e3-program/compute-provider). ## Update the integration test The template has an end-to-end test in `tests/integration.spec.ts`. It encrypts 1 and 2 and reckons it'll get their sum back. After your change, update the expected value: ```ts filename="tests/integration.spec.ts" expect(BigInt(result)).toBe(2n * (num1 + num2)) ``` Run the test with `pnpm test:integration`. Heads up: it needs a CLI knocked together from source with the `test-only-skip-proof-aggregation` Cargo feature switched on. The release binaries don't have it. See [Installation](/build/installation#install-the-cli) for how to build from source. ## Operations on ciphertexts The template uses the `fhe` crate from `gnosisguild/fhe.rs` at tag `v0.4.2`. For a `Ciphertext`, that crate gives you these operators: | Operation | Operator | Example | | --------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------- | | Add two ciphertexts | `+`, `+=` | `&a + &b` | | Subtract two ciphertexts | `-`, `-=` | `&a - &b` | | Negate a ciphertext | unary `-` | `-&a` | | Add or subtract a plaintext | `+`, `+=`, `-`, `-=` | `&a + &plaintext` | | Multiply by a plaintext | `*`, `*=` | `&a * &plaintext` | A `Plaintext` has to use the same parameters object as the ciphertext, which is `fhe_inputs.params`. If the parameters objects don't match, the operator panics and the whole thing falls in a heap. Every result wraps modulo the plaintext modulus. A negative result, say from `&a - &b` with `a < b`, wraps round to a big number. The crate also does `*` for two ciphertexts, but the default template doesn't use it and this page doesn't go there. ## Next steps Write the FHE computation for your very own E3 program. Check the inputs and verify the proofs in your E3 program contract. Find which file to tweak for each part of the template.

declined.reason: 'less than 100' is arithmetic; 'maggoted' means blind drunk. Wrong sense entirely.
'a source build' is a noun (building from source); 'a source knock together' is ungrammatical. Used 'knocked together' once for 'built' instead.
